en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Twentieth Chapter
The Discussion on Knowledge:
Is knowledge consisting of twelve bases supramundane? Yes.
Are there twelve supramundane knowledges?
One should not say so …pe… are there twelve supramundane knowledges?
“Yes.
“Are there twelve paths of stream-entry?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Are there twelve paths of stream-entry? Yes.
Are there twelve fruits of stream-entry?
It should not be stated thus … [and so on] … there are twelve paths of once-returning … [and so on] … paths of non-returning … [and so on].
Are there twelve paths to arahantship?
One should not say so … [as before] … Are there twelve paths to arahantship?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there twelve fruits of arahantship?
You should not say so … [and so on] … No.
Is it not to be said that knowledge having twelve bases is supramundane?
Yes, it is.
“Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
‘Bhikkhus, regarding these things unheard of before, there arose in me the eye, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, light arose:

“This is the noble truth of suffering. Bhikkhus, regarding this noble truth of suffering, that it must be fully understood, there arose in me the eye, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, light arose. [And so on.]
"It has been fully understood by me, monks" ...
"This is the noble truth of the origin of suffering, monks" ...
"That noble truth of the origin of suffering must be abandoned by me, monks" ... [and so on].
"It has been abandoned by me, monks" ...
"This is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, monks" ...
"That noble truth of the cessation of suffering must be realized by me, monks" ... [and so on].
“‘This has been realized by me,
monks’ … ‘This is the noble truth of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering,
monks’ … ‘This noble truth of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering must be developed by me, monks’ …” [and so on].
"‘Developed,’ monks, regarding these states unheard of before, vision arose in me … light arose,” is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes.
Therefore, knowledge based on the twelve bases is supramundane.
The Discussion of Knowledge is finished.
The twentieth chapter.
Its summary (uddāna) is:
The matricide is an immediate offense; the patricide is an immediate offense; the murderer of an arahant is an immediate offense; the shedder of [a Buddha’s] blood is an immediate offense.

"One who causes a schism in the Saṅgha is subject to immediate retribution; one who causes a schism in the Saṅgha is subject to immediate retribution. There is no knowledge in an ordinary person (puthujjana);
there are no wardens of hell in the hells; there are animals among the devas; the path has five factors; supramundane knowledge has twelve bases. The Fourth Fifty.
Its summary verse:
Suppression, the accumulation of merit, he stood, and by means of the past, the matricide.
